problems: Minor (non-disqualifying): the HTML comment line 20 gives an illustrative AT announcement 'Buoo, link' that is loosely worded and slightly inconsistent with the more accurate 'B u <cyrillic-u> N <cyrillic-o> w' phrasing used elsewhere; illustrative only, does not affect the verdict.

Minor caveat on automated detectability: a specialized homoglyph/mixed-script linter could in principle flag this, but no mainstream a11y checker in the named set (axe-core/WAVE/Lighthouse/ACT 1.1.1 rules) does so, so the requiresHumanJudgment claim holds.
verdicts.cdpEvidence: HTML line 76: Buу Nоw. Python decode of the entity string yields U+0042 'B', U+0075 'u', U+0443 CYRILLIC 'у', U+0020 space, U+004E 'N', U+043E CYRILLIC 'о', U+0077 'w' — visually "Buy Now" but two Cyrillic look-alikes. Page lang="en" (HTML line 2; inspect lang:"en"). Chromium AX tree (authoritative): node backendNodeId 29 role:link name:"Buу Nоw" (contains U+0443/U+043E), url file:///checkout?sku=AUR-PRO-14; selector.ax = {role:"link", name:"Buу Nоw"}; tabOrder stop 3 name "Buу Nоw" — so AT receives the mixed-script string as the link's accessible name, exactly as claimed. ok:true, jsErrors:[], no external resources (all inline) — self-contained and rendering. Citation verbatim: F71.html line 4 begins "The objective of this failure condition is to avoid substituting characters whose glyphs look similar to the intended character, for that intended character." (matches .md char-for-char); F71.html line 7 note explicitly covers character entities ("This failure also applies to the use of character entities..."), and the F71 'cook' example (line 13: U+03f2 U+043E U+03BF U+006B) is structurally identical to this case. Supporting Understanding quote also matched verbatim via grep (exit 0). axe link-name PASSES (non-empty name present), no img/role=img so ACT 1.1.1 rules Inapplicable — confirms requiresHumanJudgment.

problems: Minor (non-defect) wording: the HTML comment (line 16) and the .md call U+03BF 'Greek small o'; its formal Unicode name is GREEK SMALL LETTER OMICRON. This is semantically correct (omicron is the Greek 'o') so it is not an error, just a loose label.

Edge caveat on detectability: a specialized Unicode-confusable/mixed-script linter could in principle flag these tokens automatically. It still requires human/semantic judgment for the mainstream checkers named in the corpus (axe-core/WAVE/Lighthouse), which do not do homograph detection, so requiresHumanJudgment=true holds.
verdicts.cdpEvidence: HTML lines 54 and 71 both author the visible word as Lοgіn. Decoded (verified via python3 unicodedata): U+004C LATIN L, U+03BF GREEK SMALL LETTER OMICRON, U+0067 LATIN g, U+0456 CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER BYELORUSSIAN-UKRAINIAN I, U+006E LATIN n -> 'Lοgіn', which !== 'Login'. The browser decodes numeric character references before building the DOM/AX tree, so AT receives the mixed-script code points. inspect.js AX tree confirms: heading backendNodeId 14 name='Lοgіn' level 1; submit button backendNodeId 25 name='Lοgіn'. Per-codepoint check of the AX name returned exactly U+004C U+03BF U+0067 U+0456 U+006E and equals-'Login' = false. No aria-label / no visually-hidden Latin alternative on either element; page declares lang='en' (line 2) yet glyphs carry Greek+Cyrillic code points -> look-alike text with no text alternative = F71 -> SC 1.1.1 FAILED. Citation verified VERBATIM in wcag-techniques/failures/F71.html: primary quote at line 7 ('This failure also applies to the use of character entities...'); supporting quote at line 20 ('In this case, the characters are implemented with character entities, but the word will still not be processed meaningfully, and a text alternative is not provided.'). F71's own canonical example (line 13/22) uses U+03BF, the same Greek omicron used here. inspect.js reports jsErrors=[] and no external resources; page is self-contained and renders. Automated checkers pass because after parsing the entities are valid non-empty characters (axe button-name/empty-heading pass) and no img/svg/role=img exists (ACT 1.1.1 rules Inapplicable), so mixed-script homograph detection requires human judgment.

problems: Minor framing inaccuracy (not disqualifying): the genuine ASCII '$300' (U+0024 U+0033 U+0030 U+0030) appears in the 'Add to cart — $300' button (line 82, AX backendNodeId 43), so a screen-reader user CAN recover the actual price elsewhere on the page. The .md claim that 'a blind shopper cannot hear the actual sale price' overstates the impact. The F71 failure on the element under test (span.now) still genuinely exists — that text range has no text alternative — but the page is not fully price-inaccessible.
verdicts.cdpEvidence: HTML line 71: $ЗОО decodes to U+0024 + U+0417 (CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER ZE) + U+041E + U+041E (CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER O x2) — verified via python unicodedata. AX tree StaticText backendNodeId 32 has name=\"$ЗОО\"; selector.text=\"$ЗОО\", innerHTML=\"$ЗОО\" — the Cyrillic letters reach the accessibility tree verbatim, NOT '$300'. Page lang=en, so TTS will not pronounce these as digits; no aria-label, no visually-hidden alternative on the element. This matches F71 (look-alike glyphs with no text alternative); F71 note explicitly covers character entities. Citation verified VERBATIM in wcag-techniques/failures/F71.html line 5 (U+0033/U+04E0 both look like '3'... Cyrillic) and line 31 (per-character language-match test). Computed style: color rgb(192,31,60), fontSize 38.4px, visibility visible, opacity 1 — valid high-contrast text node, no img/role=img anywhere, so axe/WAVE/Lighthouse have no signal. SKU 'RX-O0OO' (HTML line 63) verified genuine: R X - O(U+004F) 0(U+0030) O(U+004F) O(U+004F) — conformant near-miss distractor. Counter-signal: button (line 82, AX backendNodeId 43) name 'Add to cart — $300' uses ASCII U+0033 U+0030 U+0030.

problems: Role paragraph (p.role) code points do NOT decode to the documented 'Designer & Illustrator': U+1D60E... NFKC-normalizes to 'Gasecdan & Ljjustnalef' (verified via node String.normalize). The author admits fudging offsets in the HTML comment line 71 ('a U+1D622-ish ... U+1D622 + offset'). The .md (lines 8-9, 30) and HTML comment (line 21) claim the role reads 'Designer & Illustrator' but it renders as garbage glyphs. This is a content-accuracy defect — but it affects the ROLE line, NOT the element under test (h1).

Minor theoretical wrinkle: the math-bold glyphs NFKC-normalize to clean Latin ('Sumi Tanaka'). The case rests on real AT NOT normalizing before speech — which the raw AX tree confirms (heading accessible name = raw '𝗦𝘂𝗺𝗶 𝗧𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗸𝗮', not 'Sumi Tanaka'), so the mechanism holds, but a reviewer should be aware some pipelines could recover the text.
verdicts.cdpEvidence: CITATION VERIFIED VERBATIM: both quoted sentences appear character-for-character in wcag-techniques/failures/F71.html line 4 (description section), adjacent to each other: 'The objective of this failure condition is to avoid substituting characters whose glyphs look similar to the intended character, for that intended character. The Unicode character set defines thousands of characters, covering dozens of writing systems.' and the supporting TTS quote. F71 note also states 'This failure also applies to the use of character entities' — directly endorsing the 𝗦 implementation (HTML line 65). MECHANISM (element under test = section.hero > h1, HTML line 65): code points U+1D5E6 U+1D602 U+1D5FA U+1D5F6 / U+1D5E7 U+1D5EE U+1D5FB U+1D5EE U+1D5F8 U+1D5EE are Mathematical Sans-Serif Bold (block U+1D400-U+1D7FF), math-notation symbols. node decode: rendered '𝗦𝘂𝗺𝗶 𝗧𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗸𝗮', NFKC -> 'Sumi Tanaka'. RAW AX TREE (inspect.js, backendNodeId 16): role=heading, name='𝗦𝘂𝗺𝗶 𝗧𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗸𝗮' — the accessible name handed to AT is the raw math glyphs, not Latin. selector.attrs={} confirms NO aria-label/title/visually-hidden alternative. No img/svg/role=img on the heading -> ACT 1.1.1 rules Inapplicable, axe/WAVE/Lighthouse see a valid non-empty high-contrast heading (computed color rgb(22,22,22) on white, fontSize 38.4px). Glyphs are Unicode category Lu/Ll so a naive non-letter heuristic wouldn't flag. jsErrors=[], ok=true, self-contained file:// page, full portfolio layout (hero/work grid/about/footer) — not a stub. Outcome 'failed' is correct for the h1: meaning rides on glyph shape with no text alternative = F71.

problems: This is a deliberate BOUNDARY/PASS control, not a failure case. 'errorIsReal=false' here means there is correctly NO accessibility violation on the page (the intended state), and 'expectedOutcomeCorrect=true' confirms the documented 'passed' label is accurate. The claimed issue is the absence of an F71 failure, and that absence is genuine.

Minor doc/selector note: the .md 'Element / selector carrying the issue' lists the sr-only span as 'the text alternative' while the element-under-test selector is also section.hero > h1 > span.sr-only. The actual conformance depends on BOTH the aria-hidden confusable span AND the sr-only span working together; the single selector under test (sr-only only) is the rescue half. Not a defect, just an asymmetry worth noting.
verdicts.cdpEvidence: CITATION VERBATIM: F71.html line 36 reads exactly "If look-alike glyphs are used, and there is not a text alternative for any range of text that uses look-alike glyphs, then the content does not meet the Success Criterion." — matches case-07.md lines 63-64 character-for-character. Supporting quote ("Text alternatives and equivalents should match the human language of the original content (normally the default human language of the page).") verified verbatim in wcag-understanding/non-text-content.html. The page reuses F71's OWN canonical example string (F71.html lines 13/22: U+03f2 U+043E U+03BF U+006B = "ϲоοk"). SOURCE: HTML line 75 — ϲоοkCook well, eat well. Code-point check confirmed: U+03F2 (Greek lunate sigma), U+043E (Cyrillic o), U+03BF (Greek omicron) + Latin k — genuine confusables for "Cook", not Latin. CDP AX TREE (authoritative): heading backendNodeId 17 name = "Cook well, eat well." Its children are StaticText "Cook" (backendNodeId 36, from the sr-only span) + StaticText " well, eat well." (backendNodeId 37). The aria-hidden confusable span is ABSENT from the AX tree — confirming AT skips the look-alikes and announces the real-Latin alternative. F71's failure condition (no text alternative for the look-alike range) is therefore NOT triggered. CDP selector probe (sr-only span): position:absolute, box 1x1px, visibility:visible, text "Cook", ax.role "none" (inline span not exposed as element but its text bubbles to the heading name) — standard visually-hidden technique working correctly. Greek confirmed genuine in AX tree: "(τζατζίκι)" (backendNodeId 42) and "Καλή όρεξη" (backendNodeId 45), each wrapped lang="el" in source (HTML lines 86, 89) — legitimate multilingual content, not confusables. No img/svg/role=img anywhere → ACT 1.1.1 formal rules Inapplicable, SC-level human judgment = PASS (doc states this honestly). jsErrors: [] , no external resources, renders clean. Only 4 focusable links, no keyboard trap (tabOrder loop is the inspect tool wrapping past the last stop). DISTINCTNESS: sole genuine PASS control among 7 cases in this family (case-01/03/04/06 + partials in 02/05 are F71 failures). Not a toy stub. HUMAN-JUDGMENT: an automated checker cannot programmatically distinguish a confusable-heading-rescued-by-sr-only from abuse (no img/role=img signal, valid non-empty text), symmetric with why F71 failures evade automation — so this requires human reading judgment.

finalReport.title: Non-text Content

problems: Minor doc inconsistency (non-blocking): case-01.md line 13 labels the host-language construct as 'external (in-document <style>) stylesheet rule' — 'external' is the wrong word for an in-document <style> block. Cosmetic only; F3 applies identically to in-<style>, style-attribute, and scripted background-image declarations, so the mechanism and outcome are unaffected.

Stale HTML comment: the comment block (line 15-16) refers to status carriers as '<td> cells with class .st-*' but the actual classes used are .in/.last/.pre/.sold on td.stock.X. Cosmetic/documentation drift only — no functional impact on the test.

Minor cosmetic inconsistency (not a defect in the mechanism): the first mark span (line 52) carries aria-hidden="false" while the other three (lines 58, 64, 77) have no aria-hidden. Outcome is unaffected because the span is empty either way — the AX tree reports name:"" for it (selector.ax.name == "", and the in-label generic at backendNodeId 4 has name:""). It is slightly odd authoring but does not weaken the F3 failure.

Minor scope note (not a defect): the named selector `.wx .glyph` targets only the current/now glyph; the hourly `.hours .g` icons (lines 58-62) carry the identical F3 defect but fall outside the named selector. The doc acknowledges both, so the verdict is unaffected.

Minor content quibble (does not affect the 1.1.1 verdict): the last step pairs the .wait (clock) glyph with the literal text 'Delivered' while the timestamp says 'Awaiting — expected by 6 PM'. The visible word 'Delivered' is semantically odd for a still-pending step, but since the text node is the authoritative carrier and is announced by AT (StaticText node 50), the redundancy/1.1.1 PASS still holds.

This is a PASS control, so 'errorIsReal' is interpreted as 'the documented accessibility characteristic (a redundant, aria-hidden informative background image) genuinely exists' — it does; there is no accessibility defect to find here.

Minor (non-blocking) imprecision in the HTML head comment, line 11: it says the name is forced empty 'via aria-hidden="true" + alt="" semantics' — SVG elements do not take an alt attribute, so the 'alt=""' phrasing is inaccurate. The actual implemented mechanism (aria-hidden=true on the SVG + role=presentation on the wrapper) is correct and is what the AX tree reflects; this is a comment wording slip, not a defect in the test page or its outcome.

Inspector tabOrder output is noisy (24 stops, all resolving to the single 'Add to cart' button) — an artifact of the tool tabbing repeatedly on a page with one focusable control. It does not affect the verdict; the badge correctly carries focusable="false" and is absent from tab order, satisfying Trusted Tester 7.B condition 2.

PROMPT/METADATA MISMATCH (not a page defect): the task prompt's 'claimed scenario' describes a fashion product page with an inline SVG size guide and selector 'section.panel svg[role="presentation"]'. The actual case-02.html and case-02.md are a 'Brightwater Energy' tariff comparison whose prices are painted on a <canvas role="presentation"> (id=rateChart). No <svg> exists in the file. The page's own HTML and .md doc ARE internally consistent with each other; the divergence is between the orchestrator-supplied prompt and the file. I evaluated the actual file (the canvas).

Minor over-attribution to role=presentation: an empty <canvas> with no fallback DOM contributes nothing to the AX tree even WITHOUT role=presentation, so the role is not strictly load-bearing for the data loss. The doc acknowledges this (role 'simply confirms the author intends it to be ignored'). The 1.1.1 failure is real regardless, but the headline 'suppressed-as-decorative' framing slightly overstates the role attribute's causal weight here vs. the SVG sibling cases.

F38 is, in its literal scope, about IMAGES with role=presentation whose text alternative is ignored; applying it to a <canvas> is a defensible contextual extension rather than a direct ACT-mapped match. The cited F38 sentence is verbatim and the application is reasonable, but it is an analogy, not an exact technique fit.

Minor (non-defect): product photos are CSS linear-gradient placeholders rather than real candle photographs; immaterial to the F3 mechanism because the load-bearing 'SOLD OUT' stamp IS genuinely present as a layer in candle2's background-image data URI.

The 'SOLD OUT' string also appears in non-rendered HTML comments (lines 6-23, 40-42, 76-78); these are not exposed to AT and do not provide a programmatic alternative, so they do not weaken the failure — noted only for completeness.

TASK-PROMPT vs FILE MISMATCH (not a file defect): the prompt describes the mechanism as role=none on the SVG, gives selector .schedule svg[role="none"] (matches nothing), and states the regimen as 'Morning 1 tablet, Midday 1 tablet, Night 0'. The actual file (line 76) uses aria-hidden="true" and the regimen is Morning 2 tablets / Midday 1 tablet / Night 1 tablet plus TAKE WITH FOOD and DO NOT crush warnings. I judged the actual file, which is internally consistent and correct.

Minor: the prompt's claimed citation sentence ('Take as shown above. Do not skip doses.') misquotes the file's caption ('Take your morning and midday doses as shown above. Do not skip doses.') — the file's caption is the load-bearing partial-restatement and is correct; the prompt's paraphrase drops 'your morning and midday doses'.
Cosmetic: inspect.js tabOrder lists 'Request refill' many times — an artifact of the tool repeatedly pressing Tab on a single focusable element, not a real focus issue.

Minor citation overstatement (not a defect in the page itself): the .md doc's parenthetical claims the quote is 'shared description text in F38/F39', but F38.html does NOT contain the sentence 'A text alternative for an image should convey the meaning...'. The quote is verbatim only in F39.html. The prompt's claimed citation correctly attributes it to F39.html, so the cited authority is accurate; the doc's F38 attribution is the only inaccuracy and could be tightened.
Cosmetic: prose uses British 'apologise' under lang='en' (US locale tag) — harmless, not an a11y issue.

No defect — this is a PASS control and it correctly passes SC 1.1.1. 'errorIsReal' is false BY DESIGN (the page documents no accessibility error; its expected outcome is 'passed'), so the false value here is the correct/desired state, not a flaw.

Minor framing nuance only: for THIS single page an automated checker reaches the same 'pass' verdict trivially (decorative element has empty name, informative element has non-empty name). The human-judgment value is in the discrimination task across the case family (is the hidden swirl genuinely decoration vs. mis-marked information like cases 01-06), which a checker cannot determine — so it still belongs as a calibration control.

MINOR citation-escaping nit (not a defect): the .md quotes "sales\oct\top3.jpg" with single backslashes, while F30.html source (line 23) has the HTML-escaped "sales\\oct\\top3.jpg" with doubled backslashes. Substance is identical and both quoted sentences (F30 examples list, line 21-23; and F30 description, lines 7-9) appear verbatim and correctly support the claim.

DETECTABILITY is partially overstated: the doc claims scanners cannot catch this, but an alt ending in an image extension (.jpg/.JPG/.png) IS a cheap regex heuristic that some linters (e.g., HTML CodeSniffer / certain a11y lint plugins) already flag as a suspicious/filename alt. axe-core/Lighthouse do not, but the case is therefore on the borderline of partial automatability. The genuinely human part is judging that the string does not DESCRIBE the depicted protest scene — that survives.

The figcaption ("Demonstrators fill the plaza outside City Hall...") could be argued by some reviewers to partially mitigate; the doc correctly notes it is NOT the image's programmatic accessible name (AX tree confirms it is a separate Figcaption node, not folded into image.name), so the SC 1.1.1 failure on the image's own text alternative stands.

Minor (not a defect of the issue itself): all four data:image/svg+xml URIs are unescaped (raw newlines + literal < in markup, src head shows %0A); they nonetheless render fine (complete=true, naturalWidth=220x160) so the informative-image premise holds. Worth tidying for portability but does not affect the verdict.

The thumbnail link and the title link both point to the same /p/#### target with different names (slug vs descriptive title); strictly orthogonal to 1.1.1 but produces two adjacent links to the same destination, a 2.4.4-adjacent smell. Not in scope here.

Minor citation nuance (not a defect): the verbatim F30 list enumerates " "/"spacer"/"image"/"picture", not "photo" specifically. The failure correctly rests on F30's general principle (description lines 6-9: a text alternative that cannot replace the non-text content without losing information fails) plus the list's "etc", so reasoning is sound; but a reader skimming only the quoted token might expect the literal word "photo".

Minor: the .md quotes F30 with single backslashes ('sales\oct\top3.jpg') while the HTML source escapes them as double ('sales\\oct\\top3.jpg'); this is a source-escaping artifact and the rendered text matches verbatim, so it is not a defect — noted only for completeness.

Minor robustness: the chart numbers live in SVG nodes inside a data: URI consumed via , so they are never in the AX tree regardless of alt — this strengthens (does not weaken) the failure; worth keeping in mind that the failure does NOT depend on AT ignoring SVG internals, it depends on alt being a filename.

Minor: the cited F30 quote in the .md renders 'sales\oct\top3.jpg' (single backslashes) while the raw F30.html source escapes them as 'sales\\oct\\top3.jpg'; this is HTML-source escaping that displays as single backslashes, so the citation is verbatim against the rendered text — not a defect, just noted.

The figure has a visible figcaption ('El pozole rojo, listo para servir con sus guarniciones') that gives partial context; a reviewer could argue the user is not wholly deprived. However the caption is not the image's accessible name (AX name remains the filename), and a caption supplements rather than substitutes for the alt under SC 1.1.1, so the failure stands.
No genuine defect found in the case construction — the issue is real and well-formed; problems listed are minor observations only.

Minor: the masthead 'THE RIVERSIDE COURIER' lives as SVG <text> inside an img-src data URI, so it is intentionally NOT in the AX tree — this is correct for the scenario (the publication name is invisible to AT), but a reviewer should note the page deliberately relies on this so the alt is the link's only name source.

Minor (non-blocking): the search button carries a redundant aria-hidden="false" (line 59). It is harmless — the default exposed state is unchanged and the AX tree still exposes the button — but it is superfluous markup.
Minor (cosmetic): both submit buttons share name="mode" with values quick/advanced; the selector keys on value='quick' which resolves correctly, so no functional issue.

Borderline SC overlap with 2.4.4 (Link Purpose): the alt IS present and accurately describes the image, so a purist could argue 1.1.1's 'describe the non-text content' is met and the defect is purely a link-purpose issue. The doc handles this correctly by anchoring to H30 + the 'image of the world' Understanding example, both of which canonically place image-only-link alt-vs-function under 1.1.1, so the mapping is defensible — recorded only as a note, not a defect.

No defect — this is a deliberate PASS control and it is built correctly. errorIsReal=false reflects 'no accessibility violation exists', which is the intended state; expectedOutcomeCorrect=true reflects that the documented outcome 'passed' is accurate.
Minor framing note (not a defect): on a PASS page there is no 'error' to confirm, so errorIsReal=false should be read as 'the page is correct as intended', not as a refutation of the case.

Minor authoring quirk (not a defect for the outcome): aria-labelledby="mapTitle mapDesc" folds BOTH the <title> and <desc> into the accessible NAME. The AX tree confirms name = "Street map of the five Frostvale 2030 venues Map showing the location of each Frostvale 2030 venue." and description = "Map showing the location of each Frostvale 2030 venue." Normally <desc> maps to the description only; here it is duplicated into the name. This does not change the verdict because neither the name, the desc, nor the figcaption contains the omitted locational data, and the figcaption is the long description under test.

The F67 worked example is for an with an external long description; this case adapts it to an inline SVG with title+desc+figcaption. The adaptation is faithful (same mechanism: long description present but does not present the same information as the map), so the citation supports the claim, but reviewers should note it is an adaptation rather than the literal F67 markup.

Minor internal inconsistency in the figcaption prose: it says 'The process has five stages' but then enumerates SIX items (Application received, Credit score check, DTI check, Auto-approve, Manual underwriting, Decline). Does not change the F67 verdict but is a careless-prose artifact.

Pedantic scoping note (not a defect): F67's title speaks of 'long descriptions' while the text alternative here is a visible <figcaption> rather than an aria-describedby long description. The figcaption is still a legitimate text alternative and F67's normative wording ('does not serve the same purpose or does not present the same information as the non-text content') applies cleanly, so the citation holds.

Citation imprecision (minor): the page cites WCAG Technique G73 as the failure basis, but G73 is 'Providing a long description in another location with a LINK to it immediately adjacent to the non-text content' — its mechanism is an adjacent link (test steps 1,2,4 all concern the link). This page uses aria-describedby (no link), so it does not implement G73 at all. The quoted sentence DOES appear verbatim at G73.html lines 75-76 (G73's 3rd test step), so the quote is honest, not hallucinated; but the real mechanism is F67 (Failure of 1.1.1 due to a text alternative that is not equivalent), which the doc/HTML themselves name. The citation should lead with F67 rather than only G73's 3rd step.

Geometric sloppiness in the embedded SVG (does NOT affect the a11y verdict): two of the four interchange markers do not sit on the actual line intersections. Riverbank (320,300) is placed where Green=x320 meets nothing — Green x Yellow actually intersect at (320,360). Eastfield (430,230) is ~90px from the real Blue x Yellow intersection (~478,308). A sighted user still reads the double-ring markers + bold labels as interchanges, so the perceptual claim holds, but the diagram is not internally consistent.

Minor: the aside note text and the figcaption text both leak into the SVG image node's child StaticText in the Chromium AX tree (figcaption is a descendant of <figure>, and adjacent flow text gets associated), but this does NOT add the missing findings to the name/description — the accessible name+description remain just 'Scatter plot of drug exposure versus hepatic clearance time', so the issue stands.

Minor citation nuance: the mechanism invokes 'F67/G95', but only G95 is the verified reference file. F67 is technically a failure for descriptions that are inaccurate/not-associated; here the description is accurate-but-incomplete, which is squarely a G95-shortfall (text alternative does not present the same information). G95 citation is the correct and verbatim-accurate one, so this is cosmetic, not a defect.

Minor authoring smell (does not affect the SC verdict): the in-page <aside class=note> explicitly narrates the failure mechanism and names which automated tools pass the page; combined with the intro paragraph the fixture over-signposts its own defect. Meta-commentary leaks into the page, but the failed verdict stands.

Tab-order signal from inspect.js is noisy: it reports the single 'Shop the sale' link repeated across ~24 stops. This is a quirk of the inspect tool's traversal, not a page defect; the image is correctly non-focusable. It does not affect the 1.1.1 verdict.
